chunks: 3695 - And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated from Khaḍir ibn ʿAmr al-Nakhaʿī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who has wealth owed to him by another man, and he denies it.

He عليه السلام said: "If he makes him swear an oath, then he has no right to take anything from him after the oath. And if he imprisons him, he has no right to take anything from him. And if he leaves him and does not make him swear, then he remains upon his right."

key_terms.اسْتَحْلَفَهُ: he asked him to swear an oath
key_terms.الْيَمِينِ: the oath used in legal denial
key_terms.فَيَجْحَدُهُ: then he denies it or refuses to acknowledge it
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or money owed as a debt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a debtor denies a debt and the creditor demands an oath?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a denied debt and the consequences of pursuing an oath or detention against the debtor. It indicates that once the creditor seeks an oath, or detains the debtor, he may no longer take anything afterward, whereas if he leaves the matter without making him swear, his claim remains.
